chunks: 9-1 Isma'il ibn Mansur al-Qassar narrated: Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan ibn Ja'far ibn al-Hasan [ibn al-Hasan] ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib عليهما السلام narrated to us. He said: Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Dimashqi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Aban narrated to us. He said: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad ibn Musa ibn 'Ubaydah narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Umm Hani' bint Abi Talib, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made Islam manifest through my hands, and sent down the Furqan upon me, and opened the Ka'bah through my hands, and favored me over all His creation, and made me in this world the master of the children of Adam, and in the Hereafter the adornment of the Resurrection, and He forbade entry into Paradise to the Prophets until I enter it, and forbade it to their communities until my community enters it, and made the caliphate in my Ahl al-Bayt after me until the blowing into the Trumpet. So whoever disbelieves in what I say has indeed disbelieved in Allah the Magnificent.

key_terms.أَهْلِ بَيْتِي: my Ahl al-Bayt, the Prophet’s household designated here for post-prophetic authority
key_terms.الْإِسْلَامَ: Islam, the religion made manifest through the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise, whose entry for prophets and nations is described in relation to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and his Ummah
key_terms.الْخِلَافَةَ: the caliphate, described as being placed in the Prophet’s Ahl al-Bayt after him
key_terms.الْفُرْقَانَ: the Furqan, meaning the revealed criterion sent down upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.الْقِيَامَةِ: the Resurrection, in which the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله is described as an adornment
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةَ: the Ka'bah, whose opening is attributed here through the Prophet’s hands
key_terms.سَيِّدَ وَلَدِ آدَمَ: the master of the children of Adam, indicating the Prophet’s supreme worldly rank

ai.seo_question: What special distinctions and authority does this hadith say Allah granted to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and his Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a series of nine distinctions granted by Allah to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, including the manifestation of Islam through him, the revelation of the Furqan to him, his superiority over creation, and his rank in this world and the Hereafter. It also affirms the continuation of authority in his Ahl al-Bayt after him until the blowing of the Trumpet, framing denial of this declaration as disbelief in Allah the Magnificent.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 9-1 Isma’il ibn Mansoor al-Qassar narrated that Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hassan ibn Ja’far ibn al-Hassan (ibn al-Hassan) ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) quoted Suleiman ibn Abdul Rahman al-Dimashqi, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Aban, on the authority of Abdul Aziz ibn Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Ubaydat, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Dinar, on the authority of Umm Hani, the daughter of Abi Talib,

that the Messenger of Allah (sw) said, “Allah, the Blessed and Sublime, propagated Islam by me, and He descended the Furqan (Quran) to me, and He conquered the Ka’ba with my hands, and He preferred me above all His creation, and He established me in this world as the Master of the Children of Adam, and He established me in the Hereafter as the adornment of the Day of Resurrection, and He forbade the entry into Paradise for all the prophets before I enter it, and He forbade the entry into Paradise for all nations until after my nation enters it, and He established the Caliphate in my Household after me until the Trumpet is blown. So whoever denies what I said has indeed denied Allah the Majestic.”
